In [[geometry]], the '''metabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|74}}}}). It can be constructed as a [[rhombicosidodecahedron]] with two non-opposing [[pentagonal cupola]]e rotated through 36 degrees. It is also a [[Midsphere#Canonical polyhedron|canonical polyhedron]].
[[File:J74 metabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a metabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron]]
{{Johnson solid}}

Alternative Johnson solids, constructed by rotating different cupolae of a rhombicosidodecahedron, are: 
* The [[gyrate rhombicosidodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|72}}}}) where only one cupola is rotated;
* The [[parabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|73}}}}) where two opposing cupolae are rotated;
* And the [[trigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|75}}}}) where three cupolae are rotated.
